title: Field Observability: SRE Weekly (Nov 27 2029)
body:
TL;DR:
- Quiet week overall but high-impact noon outage on 2029-11-25 caused ~2.4 hours of elevated error rates for hosted-api write paths due to an emergent KV-cache compaction bug plus a suboptimal autoscaler response profile for new Dedicated pools.
- Net effect: temporary 1.8% error-budget burn for hosted-api SLOs (30d window). Action items assigned and can be closed next week if fixes pass canary.

Summary and context:
This note collects shift-level observations, incident summary, SLO math for the week, and handoff flags for the next on-call rotation. We're experimenting with shorter, more field-observability-oriented updates that include raw timelines and quick triage hypotheses to reduce handoff cognitive load.

Incident highlight: KV-cache compaction + cold autoscale (2029-11-25 11:52–14:12 UTC)
- 11:51 UTC: first uptick in 5xxs on hosted-api write routes (alerts triggered: hosted-api-5xx-rate > 0.5% p95 for 5m).
- 11:52 UTC: pager -> oncall Eng-SRE (Miguel). Initial signal: sudden rise in p99 latency and write errors that correlated with a single serving cluster group in us-west-2 dedicated pools.
- 11:55–12:10 UTC: triage: stack traces pointed to KV-compression/gc path in serving runtime. Hypothesis A: compaction job thrashing under high ephemeral KV churn. Hypothesis B: compaction amplified memory pressure causing eviction storms and token duplication leading to downstream failures.
- 12:15 UTC: mitigations: disabled background compaction on affected pool via remote flag; scaled additional Dedicated workers with a faster cold-start warmup image.
- 12:45 UTC: partial recovery in p99 latency; residual errors persisted due to backlog of failed writes.
- 13:20 UTC: rolled a targeted runtime patch to short-circuit compaction when eviction pressure > 85% (hotfix PR referenced in linked_artifacts).
- 14:12 UTC: metrics returned to baseline for >30m; alert resolved.

Impact and SLO math (hosted-api write path):
- SLO target: 99.9% success over 30d for write requests (excl. maintenance windows).
- This week’s contribution: incident caused 2.4 hours of degraded success rate from 11:52–14:12 UTC on 2029-11-25. Weighted traffic factor for that cluster group = 0.42 of total writes.
- Approximate burn: 2.4 hours * 0.42 = 1.0 effective hours of full-traffic degradation. Over a 30d window (720 hours) that is ~0.14% SLO burn. Combined with two small degradations earlier this week, total weekly burn reported to SLO dashboard: 1.8% (cumulative), leaving error budget headroom of ~98.2% for the 30d window (note: separate short-window error budgets remain constrained).

Lessons learned and immediate follow-ups (short list):
1) Runtime compaction needs a safety knob: add explicit backoff to compaction when eviction > threshold (owner: Rina). ETA: PR + canary by 2029-12-03.
2) Autoscaler warmup profile: current Dedicated pool cold-start image lacks preloading for KV hot keys; create a warm image that pre-populates hot key indices and warms KV index caches (owner: Evan). ETA: 2029-12-06.
3) Improve alert fidelity: split hosted-api 5xx alert by error class (runtime vs upstream) and by pool tag to reduce blast radius and faster assignment routing (owner: Miguel). ETA: 2029-12-01.
4) Short postmortem doc: blameless timeline and RCA to be authored and linked under Confluence (owner: Asha). ETA draft by 2029-12-02.

On-call handoff notes (next rotation: Nov 28–Dec 4):
- Watchlist for next 48 hours: any resurgence of p99 latency in write routes after canary deployments; increased KV eviction rates in clusters with recent config changes; elevated cold-start errors after autoscaler adjustments.
- Key dashboards: Hosted-API Write SLO (30d), KV-cache eviction heatmap (per-pool), Dedicated autoscale event log.
- Escalation pointers: if error budget burn for hosted-api > 3% in rolling 7d, escalate to Eng-Platform lead (Slack: #eng-platform-urgent) and rotate rollback of last Dedicated image.
- Temporary mitigations to know: remote flags available to disable compaction (flag: runtime.kv.compaction.enabled=false), and autoscaler can be pinned to warm image tag warm-2029-11-20.

Operational observations and smaller notes (snapshots):
- Night shift noticed spurious 429s on embedding generation during peak on Wed (suspected upstream rate-limiter change in partner proxies). Tracking under JIRA-SRE-5021.
- Observability gap: currently we lack an alert that correlates KV eviction storms with autoscaler churn; logging team suggested a lightweight correlation job. Short-term TODO to add an anomaly pipeline to surface co-occurrence (owner: Rina).
- Runbook tweak: add a step to check Dedicated pool 'recent-roll' label before initiating autoscale (reduces false positives).

Open questions and hypothesis backlog (notes to self):
- Why did compaction get scheduled exactly at 11:52? Need inspection of compaction scheduler heuristics and whether cluster housekeeping jitter aligned.
- Could prefix caching reduce pressure sufficiently to avoid compaction? Simulation required.

Action tracker (quick table-style bullets):
- Rina: compaction backoff PR, add unit + integ test for eviction edge-case.
- Evan: build warm image and run capacity smoke tests on staging.
- Miguel: split alerts and improve pager routing.
- Asha: draft blameless postmortem and coordinate customer comms template (if we decide customer-facing note needed).

Customer-facing risk note: none published yet. Sufficient internal mitigation and rollback options available; Customer Success flagged high-usage customers who might have seen errors — reach out if required after postmortem.

Misc (working scratch):
- Rough notes from the debug session: memory map snapshots attached in incident ticket; heap profiles show compaction scanning thrash on key range shards 17–22.
- Quick grep commands used: 
  - `rg "compaction" runtime/logs | tail -n 200`
  - `kubectl logs -n serving -l pool=dedicated-usw2 | rg "eviction"`

Next sync: weekly SRE sync on 2029-12-02 16:00 PT — we'll review canary results and close action items.

Unresolved: compaction scheduler jitter root cause (Asha + Rina)

Notes-to-self style closure: keep this short at handoff; include raw timestamps and action owners to reduce re-asking during night shifts. If you add anything here during your shift, append with initials and UTC timestamp.

Appendix: recent commits and PRs related to this incident (for quick reference):
- PR #1286: short-circuit compaction on high eviction pressure (canary merged 2029-11-25).
- PR #1291: autoscaler warm-image tag bump (staged).

Document history: created by Asha Patel 2029-11-27. Last edited by Miguel Torres 2029-11-28 (minor alert routing notes).

-- end of notes --
